title: Building an Offline-First AI Coding Tutor for Low-End Android Phones
gist: Efiwe's CTO details engineering lessons from an offline-first PWA coding tutor for low-end Android phones (22,000+ learners, 160 countries): WebAssembly in a Worker, IndexedDB over localStorage, treating storage quota failure as a normal case, a two-tier hosted/on-device AI feedback contract, shared-device profiles, and a hidden-footer discoverability failure.

insights.claim: Efiwe chose a PWA over a native app because an APK is tens of megabytes before any content, service workers update on next visit while store releases leave long tails, and WebAssembly gives one runtime for Python, SQL, JavaScript and HTML.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: In data-constrained markets, web distribution removes install friction and update lag.
insights.locator: Why a PWA and not a native app

insights.claim: Learner code is executed on the device using sql.js (SQLite in WebAssembly) and Pyodide (CPython in WebAssembly), initialised lazily in a Web Worker never on the main thread, since both are large and slow to start.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Server-free code execution removes per-attempt round trips and server cost, enabling offline edtech.

insights.claim: Learner errors are treated as ordinary traffic rather than exceptions, and SQL grading compares result shape and content, not output strings, returning a reason code that drives feedback.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Failure-tolerant grading yields more useful feedback at low cost.
insights.locator: The distinction in that last block is worth dwelling on

insights.claim: localStorage was the wrong cache for translated content: it is capped around 5 MB per origin, throws QuotaExceededError, and is synchronous, blocking the main thread on slow-flash, low-end devices.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Synchronous storage hides a main-thread cost on the hardware that can least afford it.
insights.locator: We started that cache in localStorage

insights.claim: Migration to IndexedDB used a dual-read window (read new store, fall back once to legacy, promote, delete legacy key) with every legacy read and promotion write wrapped, to avoid stranding offline users.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.locator: Choosing IndexedDB was the easy part.

insights.claim: A full storage volume is a normal operating condition on low-end devices, and a single uncaught awaited cache write in the course startup path produced a blank screen for Nigerian pilot students; the fix made persistence fire-and-forget with an explicit catch.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Never gate rendering on persistence success; cheap devices cluster failures through small storage, not hardware incompatibility.
insights.quote: persistence calls in a startup path are fire-and-forget with an explicit catch, never awaited
insights.locator: Storage quota as a first-class failure mode

insights.claim: navigator.storage.estimate() returns padded, approximate values for privacy, so Efiwe uses it only as a planning signal to decide between full precache and lazy fetch, with 25% headroom.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Storage quota APIs are not guarantees; design defensively.

insights.claim: Efiwe's AI feedback uses a hosted model within a 4-second timeout and falls back to a deterministic on-device analysis plus a local model; the local analysis always runs first and is passed as context to the hosted request, giving a smaller, more consistent prompt.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: A defined second tier, timeout and recorded tier is the template for AI features that must survive poor connectivity.
insights.locator: Two-tier AI feedback and an honest degradation contract

insights.claim: navigator.onLine is only a fast negative signal because it reports a network interface, not reachability, so the timeout is what protects learners on captive portals or stalled connections.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Timeouts, not connectivity flags, define graceful degradation.
insights.locator: navigator.onLine is checked but never trusted.

insights.claim: AI feedback on wrong answers was Efiwe's highest-rated feature at 4.3 of 5 in the Nigerian pilot, with nine of ten educators scoring it 4 or 5.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Personalised feedback is the demonstrated value driver in low-resource education.
insights.locator: Efiwe gives every learner personalised feedback

insights.claim: Early binary feedback was unactionable without a teacher, so Efiwe added a deterministic Levenshtein-based proximity hint giving character-level nudges for near-misses and conceptual explanations otherwise, which works offline.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Deterministic feedback logic reduces dependence on model quality.

insights.claim: On-device model quality is the real ceiling on offline feedback, and the approach works because coding challenges have checkable answers; a softer domain would not have that fallback.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Offline AI tutoring is viable for verifiable domains first.
insights.locator: On-device model quality is the real ceiling

insights.claim: Efiwe has had more than 22,000 learners across 160 countries, serves content in 246 languages, and ran structured pilots in Lagos and Ogun State (Nigeria) and Uttarakhand (India); one cohort of 80 students produced 6 graduates before the redesign.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Early traction in underserved edtech markets; dropout was driven by connectivity, not intent.
insights.locator: Out of one cohort of 80 enrolled students

insights.claim: In the Nigerian pilot eight of ten educators cited students lacking personal devices as the dominant obstacle, so Efiwe supports up to twenty saved profiles per device with local stores namespaced by profile.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Shared-device support is an architectural requirement in these markets; retrofitting is costly.
insights.locator: Multi-user devices are an architectural requirement

insights.claim: Offline reliability scored 4.0 of 5 in Nigeria and every low score traced to connectivity dropping before the first caching cycle finished, a first-run sequencing failure fixable by prioritising the minimum offline payload.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Prioritise the minimum viable offline payload on first run.
insights.locator: Two deployments gave us the evidence base

insights.claim: Four of ten educators never tried the local-language interface because the control sat in the page footer, showing a demonstrated feature can be functionally invisible; discoverability differs from usability.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Test whether users will encounter a feature in their actual path.
insights.quote: Discoverability and usability are not the same property.
insights.locator: The finding that stung most was about language

insights.claim: WebAssembly runtime cold start remains poor on the weakest devices, and storage stays adversarial: quota is padded, eviction opaque and persist() inconsistent across browsers, so defensive coding is a workaround for a platform gap.
insights.speaker: Chidi Nwaogu
insights.so_what: Browser storage guarantees are a constraint for offline-first products.
